\[
I_{\text{out}}(p) = \frac{\sum_{q \in \Omega_p} w(p,q)\, I(q)}{\sum_{q \in \Omega_p} w(p,q)},
\qquad
w(p,q) = e^{-\frac{\lVert p - q \rVert^2}{2\sigma_s^2}}\; e^{-\frac{d(I(p),\, I(q))^2}{2\sigma_r^2}}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(\sigma_s\): The spatial sigma in pixels
- \(\sigma_r\): The range sigma in 8-bit levels
- \(d\): The difference in one channel, or the distance between RGB colors
- \(\Omega_p\): The disk-shaped window around p

The weight of a neighbor q is the product of two Gaussians. The first falls with the distance between the pixels, the second with the difference d between their values. Neighbors across an edge have a large d, so they get almost no weight, and the edge stays. Omega_p is the disk of radius ceil(3 sigma_s) around p, the window of OpenCV's bilateralFilter.
